To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the flow rate in the collateral artery and the zeroth order pressure in the aneurysmal region can be computed explicitly, (ii) these quantities are independent on the geometry of the stent and (iii) the flow rate and the zeroth pressure in the aneuysm are inversely proportional to the flow rate in main artery.

(i) the pressure in the aneurysmal cavity is equal to the average pressure along the stented artery; (ii) the velocity profile through the stent can be approximated by a linear function of the input/output pressure drop, and the pressure drop can be approximated as the product of the flow-rate and of the stented artery length

(i), the flow-rate through the collateral artery can be computed explicitly from the input/output pressures, (ii) in an aneurysm the stent modifies the vortex rotation, (iii) the zeroth-order term of the pressure inside the aneurysmal vessel is equal to the averaged pressure along stent in the artery, (iv) the first order approximation of the flow is explicit and is first-order accurate, (v) the first order pressure approximation is implicit
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the blood-flow in a stent.
the study of the hemodynamics of blood flow in stented arteries, with particular emphasis on the modeling of the stent as a multi-layered structure.
the development of a new asymptotic approach that allows us to model the flow-rate in a collateral artery and the pressure distribution in a sac connected to a stent.
